p: The ad demonstrates a workflow where a user comments directly on an online document, invokes an AI agent via terminal to apply the feedback, and immediately sees the same URL updated with the changes and the comment marked resolved.
Artifact Share lets teams annotate generated HTML docs and have AI agents update the live document directly at the original URL.

p: ["off-target scenario: reads as generic decision-doc/PM workflow, not an AI-coding-agent artifact demo","product branding absent until the final card; four of five frames could be any doc tool","'any agent' claim never shown — only Claude Code branding appears ('Drafted by Claude Code', 'claude -p'), which undercuts the multi-agent promise","'same URL' loop is implied but never made visually explicit (no URL bar/persistent link shown)","hook text diverges from stated concept ('Humans point. Agents edit.') and is low-urgency for a scrolling dev audience"]

The demo clearly walks through comment → AI edit → republish → decision, and the mocked doc UI is clean and legible with no rendering defects. But it plays like a generic enterprise decision-doc case study rather than an artifact-sharing tool for AI coding agents, and the only visible agent branding is Claude Code, which contradicts the intended 'any agent, same URL' differentiator. Product identity (artifactshare.com) only appears in the last of five frames, so salience and hook strength both suffer for a fast X scroll.
